Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8181050
Permit API: 125-28761
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: North Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/26/2024
Comments: On 03/26/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Fowler Well Site following routine complete inspections that were conducted for each well on 01/03/2024 (See IR 3670374 for example). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainee Olivia Holley (PA DEP). It was noted that sediment was being transported towards the main township road, Little Daniel's Run Road, down the side of the road to a storm grate. Sediment was accumulating within the rock lined channel and pooling at the base of the channel, adjacent to the access road.It was discussed with EQT via phone for plans to install a rubber belting water bar to divert the spring water towards the rock lined channel instead of flowing down the center of the access road. EQT also used dust suppressant on the road. The following was observed during inspection on 03/26/2024:The rubber belting water bar was not yet installed on the access road. The access road displayed some dust suppressant, however I recommend that additional is applied, focusing on the beginning of the access road where the spring is out letting and the water is leaving the site. There was a section of dust suppressant at the top of the road near the tanks, however it was unclear if this area was existing (Photos 1-6).Newly installed storm grate at the base of the rock lined channel was in generally good condition. Some sediment accumulation noted on the bottom. No sediment noted within stone around the storm grate coming from the stabilized bank or the channel (Photos 7, 8).Sediment was accumulating along the base of the access road and main township road which appeared to be originating from the site. This sediment was leading towards the storm grate along the main township road. Sediment did not appear to be accumulating within the storm grate (Photos 9-12).Sediment laden water leaving the access road was noted leading towards the township storm grate. Some rills were noted within the sediment (Photos 13-18).The channel on the property across the street where the township storm grate and culvert outlets did not appear to be accumulating sediment from the access road (Photo 19). Overview of access road, storm grates and outlet across the street leading to Little Daniels Run (Photo 20).Due to the continuing discharge of sediment laden water off of the access road and sediment accumulation of sediment along the main township road, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), and 78a.53 are being issued.

Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2017-03-17 to Cnx Gas Co Llc in Brady Twp, Clearfield county. 78.85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - Operator failed prevent gas flow in the annulus and use gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries in areas of known shallow gas producing zones.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Cnx Gas Co Llc
Violation Type Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date 2017-03-17
Violation Code 78.85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - Operator failed prevent gas flow in the annulus and use gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries in areas of known shallow gas producing zones.
Violation ID 781063
Permit API 033-26740
Unconventional N
County Clearfield
Municipality Brady Twp
Inspection Type Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date 2017-03-17
Comments Inspection of CNX’s Hartzfeld 9 (033-26740) conventional gas well in Brady Twp., Clearfield County conducted March 17, 2017 at 10:30 am. Yesterday the operator called to report gas noted outside the 7” csg. Today we met on location to go over the well’s condition, see where integrity issues are noted, and discuss any possible migration pathway to surface. At the time of inspection; 13 3/8” x 7” annulus was open to atmosphere with audible bubbling. The 7” x 4 ½” annulus was capped with a hammer union, (1) side outlet was open to atmosphere with notable flow of gas. The 4 1/2” csg was open to production line (~50 PSI) through side outlet. The well was previously producing through (1”) tbg string which is now shut-in/isolated from production line at a ball valve on the wellhead. The 4 ½” production casing was shut-in during that time. Integrity issues were noted after the 4 1/2” casing was opened-up and turned inline to production. Violation of 25 PA Code Ch.78.85 Cementing Standards cited given the obvious integrity issue with this well. § 78.85. Cement standards. (a) When cementing surface casing or coal protective casing, the operator shall use cement that meets or exceeds the ASTM International C 150, Type I, II or III Standard or API Specification 10. The cement must also: (1) Secure the casing in the wellbore. (2) Isolate the wellbore from fresh groundwater. (3) Contain any pressure from drilling, completion and production. (4) Protect the casing from corrosion from, and degradation by, the geochemical, lithologic and physical conditions of the surrounding wellbore. For wells employing coal protective casing, this includes, but is not limited to, formulating cement to withstand elevated sulfate concentrations and other geochemical constituents of coal and associated strata which have the potential to adversely affect the integrity of the cement. (5) Prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used. The operator appears to a have reported the issue to the Department in a timely matter in adherence to 25 PA Code Ch.78.86 Defective Casing or Cementing. In accordance to 78.86, at this point the operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § § 78.91—78.98. Also noted at the time of inspection was a monitoring well ~50 yards from the well. I lifted the well cap and checked for gas with an Altair 5x gas meter, no gas detected in any amount at this time.

Violation(s)
ID: 781063 Date: 2017-03-17 Type: Environmental Health & Safety
78.85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - Operator failed prevent gas flow in the annulus and use gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries in areas of known shallow gas producing zones.
Enforcement Action(s)
IDCode

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 984027
Permit API: 015-23722
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Leroy Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/03/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "SGL12 M North B" Marcellus well site.Chesapeake hydraulically fractured the 4 Marcellus wells here in November 2022.Danielle Schaad called the DEP yesterday to report an estimated 1 barrel release of production liquid to the pad surface.I spoke with Danielle Schaad and Chris Lee (both Chesapeake) on site. Lee discovered production liquid in the yellow takeout can, and moist soil around the production tank yesterday. They explained that two days ago a vac truck caused the release of production liquid while transferring it from the tank, but did not report it to Chesapeake. MR Dirt is excavating the moist pad material around the production tank. Creston Environmental and I screened the moist soil around the tank for electrical conductivity (EC) with Hanna Groline Soil Test probes. Both probes maxed out (>4.00 mS/cm). Pad material not impacted by the spill is frozen solid, and we could not get EC readings from it. Chesapeake plans to remove the production tank on Monday February 23 to excavate any impacted pad material under it. The production liquid will flow into 4 GasBuster tanks in the mean time.Violations for the spill are cited to the 015-23722 permit.Cannot assess soil stabilization today because of ~2" of snow coverage. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. I did not see any pooled water on site, just snow/ice.Air temp 8FJLP

Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. Conductivity readings were taken in the vegetation that is now impacted by sediment laden waters and they are as follows: 0.410 mS in the sediment laden puddle created from the flow going off the shoulder of the road, 0.464 mS in the vegetation adjacent to where the previous puddle reading was taken, 0.502 mS in some vegetation that is further in the intermittent tributary, and lastly 0.157 mS upslope of the Act 9 sign as a background reading. Though these readings subjugate that freshwater is being released, it is evident that sediment is still entering Waters of the Commonwealth. While onsite, the Department notified John Hulsey about the sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth and advised them to promptly cease all water release dust suppression activities on the access road.The Department recommends the Operator re-evaluate their dust suppression methods or implement measures to prevent sediment laden water from entering the intermittent unnamed tributary to Miller's Run.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the discharge of sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth.

Code Chapters 78 & 102. The following was observed during the Department's inspection: 1. The well was stable and producing, with the pit having been previously reclaimed. The 23 December 2019 inspection of the site indicated that the area was, ‘snow covered and stable…appeared that temporary stabilisation measures will need to be used when weather allows'. 2. Madeley and Sheriff observed a lack of uniform vegetative cover at the site - with no evidence of seed or mulch having been placed. The pit appeared to have deformities as well and was not shaped in such a way as to prevent the pooling of water. 3. Madeley and Sheriff noted the presence of a well permit attached to a nearby tree but no evidence of a site tag on the pump jack or wellhead. 4. Mr James Highhouse arrived on-site during the inspection and told Sheriff and Madeley that he was going to immediately lay mulch about the area. Mr Highhouse also made reference to the presence of a mini-excavator already near the site and said he would be using the machine to grade the pit area for better stabilisation. 5. Sheriff and Madeley expressed their intention to have a look at other wells in the area whilst inspecting and Mr Highhouse said he would be attaching site tags to the Oakland 11 and other nearby pump jacks immediately. Madeley and Sheriff observed Mr Highhouse attaching signs to the Oakland 11 and Oakland 12 (123-48277) pump jacks. Comments: On April 28, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3966229 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding, as the start of remediation was postponed to the day of this inspection due to forecasted inclement weather. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth were observed during the time of IR 3966229, and the impacted area was covered with plastic sheeting in preparation for the weather.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5). What appears to be a covered excavation stockpile was observed onsite, which may be from remediation work that has been conducted thus far (see photo 6). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank during the time of IR 3965337 remains covered with plastic sheeting, and appears to have been excavated near the brine tank (see photos 7, 8, and 11). A soil conductivity reading was taken adjacent to the brine tank where it appears that impacted material was removed (see photo 9). Although the soil conductivity in this location did not appear to be elevated above that of the surrounding soil, some staining remained on the conductivity meter (see photo 10). Therefore it appears that additional excavation may be necessary in this location. Oil absorbent booms remain placed downslope of the covered impacted area (see photos 12 and 13). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected down slope of impacted area (see photos 14 and 15).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remediation work has begun and the impacted area remains adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater. However, the Department recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the excavated area adjacent to the brine tank for any additional remediation that may be needed.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8159691
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 2/21/23.

Inspection Date: 5/15/2025
Comments: On May 15, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3944466, where violations were left outstanding due to no Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3944466, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (see photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2-5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head was not observed on the ground during this inspection. The Department recommended in IR 3944466 that this top hatch be replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater.The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (see photos 1 and 4). The access road remains stabilized with gravel. The well tag that was affixed to the well head during the time of IR 3944466 appears to have been removed. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 6). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (see photo 7). The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site. The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (see photos 8 and 9).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued from IR 3944466 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8249813
Permit API: 117-20505
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Charleston Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: On 9/18/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a follow-up incident inspection in response to complaint #389073 at the Seneca Vandergrift 290 well site located in Charleston Twp, Tioga Co. It was 46 degrees and mostly cloudy when I arrived on site. Rainfall has not impacted the region in the last 48 hours.There are four active wells on site staged for production along with two that are in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H and 5H wells have had recent plugging operation and a plugged well monument has been installed on the 2H well, plugged date 12/4/2024. The area that was excavated around and north of the well cellars remains open along with the areas on the fill slope and across the grassy field north of the pad. Elevated conductance above 4000 uS was found in soils in the bottoms of the 2H, 3H, 5H, and 6H well cellars. The highest reading found in the 4H well cellar was 1385 uS conductance in the soil and 1035 uS conductance in the water. The highest reading witnessed in the 1H well cellar was 1230 uS conductance. Elevated conductance readings were also found at the north edge of the pad, above the east and west excavated areas of the fill slope. I did witness a wet area of soil 10 feet up from the base of the fill slope and within the approximate center of the west excavated area that field tested above 4000 uS conductance. Liquid flowing down through the excavated area below the fill slope and into the catch basin sump field tested at 1229 microsiemens conductance. Liquid in the sump field tested at 1481 microsiemens conductance and liquid flowing out of the sump field tested at 1693 microsiemens conductance.Temporary compost filter socks that were installed at the base of the fill slope and in the excavated area of the field on the north side of the location that do have sediments above 50% of the height of the sock. Temporary stabilization that has been applied to the fill slope and the excavated area of the field needs to be refreshed. Erosional channels were evident on the fill slope and within the excavated area of the the field.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 399274 and 4029808 for a release of an unknown amount of produced water to the unprotected pad surface, to the unprotected grassy field below the fill slope and flowing offsite during plugging operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance on the well pad, in the excavated areas around the well cellars, in seeps from the fill slope, in the collection sump at the northwest corner of the location and other areas on the location as discovered.4. Assess the temporary compost filter socks and temporary stabilization. Apply maintenance as necessary.I left the site at 1130 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 922305
Permit API: 125-27785
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/28/2021
Comments: On June 28, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Papa Bear Well Site in Somerset Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of fluid reported to the Department on 6/25/2021. On 6/25/2021, the Operator reported that more than 5 gallons of produced water was spilled to the well pad from a Gas Production Unit dump line. At the time of inspection, SPSI and Moody and Associates were in the process of remediating the impacted material and flushing the well pad drains. The Moody and Associates representative Jona Stosky indicated that the operator would be utilizing Act 2 clean up standards for brine. The remediation crew has excavated the well pad drain trench on the east side of the well pad. The trench was excavated directly behind the Gas Production Units (GPU). The trench appeared to be 5’ wide, 45’ long and approximately 3’ in depth. Ms. Stosky indicated that approximately 90 yards of impacted material has been removed from the well pad and placed in roll off disposal boxes. Ms. Stosky indicated that additional material may need to be removed to remediate the well pad. I observed staining on the dump line associated with the GPU labeled as the 10H. The remediation crew was flushing and or washing the well pad drain and the area under the 10H GPU unit with fresh water to flush out the production fluid. On 6/29/2021, I spoke with EQT representative David Crayne., Mr. Crayne indicated that approximately 42 gallons of production fluid was released. The spill appeared to be contained on the well pad. Violations are being issued in relation to the release of a regulated material.

Comments: On March 6, 2024, inspection conducted in response to a complaint (CTS-374226) on the Terence Shaffer 1-P041 well in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The following was observed:The well site was flooded by rainwater at the time of inspection (see photos 4 and 13). This did not appear to result in sedimentation on the well site during the time of inspection. The well site exhibited less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. A gas odor was detected onsite. Hissing and bubbling was observed coming from the well head (see photos 2 and 3). The well API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 6). However, the onsite posting lacked the operator's address. Little to no vegetative growth coverage was observed on the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 7 and 8). A cotton-like substance was observed stuffed into one of the brine tank valves, with water flowing out of this valve (see photo 9). No elevated conductivity readings were detected underneath either brine tank valve, or anywhere onsite (see photos 5, 11, 12, and 14). Tire rutting that was severely eroded to bare stone was observed in the access road entrance (see photo 15). Sediment-laden pooling was observed in these ruts at a low point in the access road (see photo 16). An apparent stream or tributary flows through a culvert underneath this point in the access road. This sediment-laden pooling could be observed flowing from the access road ruts into this apparent stream/tributary at the culvert outlet, resulting in a discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photos 17 and 18). Department vehicles were not used to access the well site or access road for this inspection.The Department recommends that the operator post their address onsite, as is required by current regulations. OGI follow-up is being requested for evaluation of well integrity.Violations are being issued against the brine tank onsite, as it appears that it would fail to keep production fluids contained. Additional violations are being issued for failing to permanently stabilize the well site and access road, resulting in a sediment-laden discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: Inspection Report 1 of 2On 03/03/2026, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the John Hunter Well Site in Donegal Township, Washington County (37-125-28285). I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Sara Trio (PA DEP).The following was observed:-Act 9 sign (Photo 1).-Sediment-laden water flowing from access road and site to culvert inlet (Photos 2-4). Recommend access road maintenance.-Culvert inlet pipe receiving road fines and sediment-laden water (Photos 5,6).-Culvert outlet area appears to be pooling/discharging sediment; visible from access road (Photos 7,8). Recommend maintenance and adequately functioning environmental controls design and application in all drainage areas.-Accelerated erosion flow path downslope from culvert outlet (Photos 9-11).-Existing Compost Filter Sock (CFS) appears overtaken by wood debris and vegetation; sediment deposition from what appears to be significant flow downslope (Photos 12,13). Report Details

Comments: On January 8, 2026, the Department conducted a Site Restoration Inspection of INR Operating LLC's Coastal Well Pad located in Springhill Township, Fayette County after a Post-Drilling Site Restoration Report (PDSRR) submission the DEP received on 12/17/2025 (Final well drilled: 10H 051-24726 Drilling Completed on: 8/27/2021.) In accordance with 78a.65, within 9 months after the completion of drilling a well or expiration of the permit for the last well drilled, the Operator shall restore the well site and submit a PDSRR within 60 days of restoration. 9 months after the completion of drilling for the last well drilled at the Coastal Well Site is 5/27/2022, therefore a PDSRR should have been submitted to the Department by 7/26/2022.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 Sign at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. The Department recommends the Operator update the sign so that other signage is not obstructing the reflective border in accordance with 78a55. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a paved access road leading to the graveled Coastal Well Pad. On the left hand side of the access road the Department observed Wet Pond #2 and it's Emergency Spillway both of which appear to be installed and functioning according to site plans. Further up the access road and on the left hand side, the Department observed Wet pond #1 and it's Sediment Forebay, both of which appeared to be installed and function according to site plans. 4 Infiltration Berms were observed to be installed next to Wet Pond #2 and #1 as depicting on the site plans. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed all perimeters of the well site to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and no erosion and sediment control features installed. At the time of this inspection, the Coastal Well Site had 2 gravel pads within its Limit of Disturbance, one of which had 4 producing wells on it and the other had 3 producing wells on it. The first well pad with 4 producing wells on it also had 8 production tanks within secondary containment, 7 GPUs within secondary containment, and other production equipment on site. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of any of the 10H's associated production equipment. The 10H wellhead had a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it. No surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the 10H wellhead. No other production equipment was observed on the second gravel pad that had 3 producing wells on it. No equipment that appears to be associated with drilling of the well was observed to be present on site.Based on today's inspection, the Coastal well site appears to be restored, therefore, the Department is recommending the Approval of the PDSRR. In addition, due to the PDSRR being submitted on 12/17/2025 which is after the 7/26/2022 deadline, violations are being noted and immediately corrected for failure to submit a PDSRR within 60 days of post drilling restoration.

Accompanying me was CNX representative Chad Eisenman.According to Department records, completion of drilling last occurred on 2/22/2025 (125-29137). Post-drilling restoration was required by 11/19/2025. The WSRR was due on 1/18/2026.The following was observed:-The Act 9 signage and mailbox including all required documentation were at site entrance (Photo 1).-Site entrance and access road appear in generally good condition (Photos 2,3).-Pad overview (Photo 4).-Eastern berm showing containment matting for temporary water line (Photo 5).-North, East, and Southern slopes appear well-vegetated with at least 70% vegetated coverage capable of resisting accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6-10).-Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) managed release pond number 1 and outlet pipe appear in good condition and functioning as well as both outlet pipes and level spreader (Photos 11-14).-Western slope as well as stockpiles per plans appear well-vegetated with at least 70% vegetated coverage capable of resisting accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 15-17).-Slopes upside of access road and the opposite small portion of berm with applied temporary straw mulch stabilization was reported by operator to be the areas of concern which prompted the period extension request; slopes appear vegetated; berm along road will be monitored and maintained as needed (Photos 18-20).Based on the site inspection, it appears that the Operator has undertaken restoration in accordance with 78a65(b) and developed in accordance with active ESCGPESG076322011,however the Operator failed to submit the WSRR in accordance with 78a65a(1)i. Violation is issued as immediately corrected.I recommend that the well site restoration extension is approved. The post-drilling well site restoration shall be completed by 11/19/2027 and the Well Site Restoration Report shall be submitted by 1/18/2028.

Comments: On July 10, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of Monona's Stickle 1H well site located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County. Accompanying on today's inspection is Tyler Metzger (WQS DEP).At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance, the Department recommends the Operator replace the Act 9 Sign with one that satisfies 78a55(i)4ii. In the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan, however it had a different Operator's name posted on it, the Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site perimeters appeared to be exhibiting at last 70% uniform and adequate vegetative cover.At the time of this inspection, the Stickle 1H well site appeared to have 2 wells on it, the 1H (permit number 129-28411) had a well tag fixed to the wellhead with the well's name and permit number on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead.A plethora of production equipment that did not appear to equipped for production was observed in several locations of the well site, the Department recommends all equipment not currently in use be removed from the well site.2 production tanks were observed to be within a secondary containment that had a minimal amount of fluid pooled in it as well as an unlabeled barrel. The production tanks appeared to be heavily corroded with several holes observed at the top of the tank located on the right-hand side. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tanks to ensure further corrosion and a release of production fluids does not occur. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed several areas of the graveled well pad to have an oily substance on it, specifically in areas relating to the reported re-plugging of the 129-28648 well. Violations were issued against the 129-28648 well for a release(s) of an oily substance.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the Act 9 Sign not in compliance, the outdated ERP and for the corrosion holes in the production tank.
